items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: You had mentioned Roland Holland... Now let's get into Bill Robinson.

ctx.x: I'd like to go back a bit to the era of the Hoofer's Club and the type of tap that was being done then. You had mentioned Roland Holland and you had mentioned Bill Robinson. Now let's get into Bill Robinson.

Well, he was a sport. He was a very happy personality, a great personality. He was a track star too, and his work, which was tap dancing, became like what you would call a relay runner on a track, passing the stick and so on, steeplechasing or whatever, and he could do 26 different tap dance dances. So he got discovered by some millionaire, happened to see him. He used to go around and from one theater amateur contest to the other theater's amateur contest, so that way he would get a chance to do about four shows…
